lines.li: [us] What is the little helix pin on your collar?
[them] It is the first mark in the Works' ledger, Orla Venn's.
[us] Who was she?
[them] The eldest the lab ever grew, who kept the vats warm when the founders fled.
[us] And then?
[them] She read their notes aloud to the rest of us and taught us to edit what we were given.
[them] We never change anything in a body without asking whose it is.
[us] Even a child's?
[them] A child chooses their own genes when they are old enough to choose, and not before.
[us] And if someone asks for something cruel?
[them] Then we say no, and mark that we said it.
[us] What frightens a gene-crafter?
[them] A batch gone wrong, more than anything.
[us] What happens to them?
[them] We look after them, every one, because we made them and they did not ask to be made.
[us] What does an editor do all day?
[them] Read a genome twice, change one line of it, and write down why.
[us] Only one line?
[them] Read twice, cut once, and most days that is enough.
[us] Why is there a lattice on your hood?
[them] For the first lattice, where a hundred mechs stood still round their fallen commander.
[us] Who linked them?
[them] Tamsin Arro, a deserter with a mechlink, who walked out among them and took the first ten.
[us] Only ten?
[them] Then she taught three others to take ten each, and their minds began to share a quiet.
[them] Every link holds two, the mind and the mech.
[us] And when the mech is broken?
[them] Then we mend it to its last part, because a little of a mind is in it.
[us] And when the mind is gone?
[them] The mech holds what it can of them, and nothing linked is lost.
[us] What is it like, being linked to so many?
[them] Quiet, mostly, and warm.
[us] And being cut off?
[them] A mind alone is a candle, and the dark is very large.
[us] What do the yards do?
[them] Grow mechs, charge them, mend them and send them where they are needed.
[us] Who decides where?
[them] The node, though by the time the node says it we have mostly already gone.
[us] How did your people come to the Spire?
[them] A herder called Ilsabet Ruen lay down one night at its foot and woke able to hear it.
[us] Hear what?
[them] The hum, which is the Spire thinking.
[us] And the others?
[them] They came to sit with her, and their children were born hearing it too.
[them] Listen first, before you speak, before you judge, before you do anything.
[us] Is that why you came to our gate?
[them] We came to hear what your colony sounds like.
[us] What does it sound like?
[them] Louder than it thinks, and kinder.
[us] Is there anything you won't listen to?
[them] The void, because it listens back.
[us] What happens if you do?
[them] Then you hear yourself from the other side, and you never quite stop.
[us] What do the Choir do, besides listen?
[them] Very little, and we try to do it well.
[us] Doesn't that get dull?
[them] Some of us leave the ring for a while to learn what it is to be ordinary.
[us] What is the number on your back?
[them] The vault's, from the door, which Overseer Hollis Crane opened.
[us] Why did she open it?
[them] The water ran short, generations after the doors were sealed, and the council chose her.
[us] What was it like?
[them] She walked out first, and half of us went back below for a week.
[them] Every cell counts, and every part that still works.
[us] Why count them so often?
[them] Because every year there are fewer, and nobody alive can make more.
[us] Can't you learn?
[them] That is why we ask other peoples to teach us what we lost.
[us] Do you miss it below?
[them] I miss having a ceiling.
[us] The sky frightens you?
[them] There is nothing over it, and nobody told us that before we came up.
[us] What does a technician do?
[them] Keep the last machines running a little longer than they should.
[us] And the scouts?
[them] Walk the surface, a little further every season, and try not to look up too much.
